$comment: Quick-example inputs for the converter UI (spec §8.1, §8.2). Every spec §8.2 example is present. Each input parses via getConverter().convertText(...) without an unknown-unit/unknown-fuel error (tests/examples.test.ts). context_required results (e.g. electricity, or a mass/volume with no fuel) are expected and OK — they are not parse failures. Fuel phrases use names/aliases from data/fuels.json. Envelope: { $comment, examples: [...] }. See src/lib/data/schemas.ts (exampleSchema).

examples.label: 1 kWh
examples.notes: Kilowatt-hour → MJ, BTU, toe/boe/tce equivalents. Exact SI energy conversions.

examples.label: 1 MWh
examples.notes: Megawatt-hour = 3.6 GJ exactly.

examples.label: 1 MJ
examples.notes: Megajoule → kWh, BTU, etc. Exact.

examples.label: 1 GJ
examples.notes: Gigajoule → kWh, MMBTU, toe. Exact.

examples.label: 1 BTU
examples.notes: International Table BTU = 1055.05585262 J (standard definition).

examples.label: 1 MMBTU
examples.notes: Million BTU = 1 dekatherm. Common in gas markets.

examples.label: 1 therm
examples.notes: US therm = 100,000 BTU_IT (standard definition).

examples.label: 1 toe
examples.notes: Tonne of oil equivalent = 41.868 GJ (IEA convention; not a real oil property).

examples.label: 1 boe
examples.notes: Barrel of oil equivalent = 5.8 MMBTU convention (~6.1 GJ). NOT a physical barrel.

examples.label: 1000 kcal
examples.notes: 1 kcal (IT) = 4186.8 J. Note food 'Calorie' = kcal.

examples.label: 1 L diesel
examples.notes: Volume + mass (density) + energy (LHV/HHV) + CO2/CO2e emissions for diesel.

examples.label: 1 L gasoline
examples.notes: Petrol: mass, energy, and CO2/CO2e emissions per litre.

examples.label: 1 L heating oil
examples.notes: Heating oil (Fuel Oil grade): mass, energy, emissions.

examples.label: 1 barrel crude oil
examples.notes: Physical barrel of crude → volume, mass and energy. Energy is an ESTIMATE (grade varies); not the same as boe.

examples.label: 1 m³ natural gas
examples.notes: Natural gas m³ → kWh with a mandatory billing/reference-condition warning (not an exact identity).

examples.label: 1 kg hydrogen
examples.notes: Hydrogen mass → energy (LHV/HHV). Direct combustion CO2 = 0 (combustion only; upstream not included).

examples.label: 1 kg hard coal
examples.notes: Hard coal (DESNZ industrial) mass → energy + CO2e. No density → no volume conversion.

examples.label: 1 kg lignite
examples.notes: Lignite (IPCC global default) → energy (wide range) + CO2. Highly variable moisture.

examples.label: 1 kg wood pellets
examples.notes: Wood pellets mass → energy, Scope-1 CO2e, and separate biogenic CO2 line.

examples.label: 1 kWh electricity
examples.notes: Electricity → energy (exact SI conversions) plus emissions marked context_required (no single global grid CO2e factor; pick a region/year). Illustrative UK 2025 and EU-27 2023 examples are shown, clearly labeled as non-default (rulebook §C.6).

examples.label: 1 kWh to MJ
examples.notes: Ask for one specific unit: the requested answer is highlighted, the other groups still follow.

examples.label: 5 kW for 3 h
examples.notes: Power becomes energy only with an explicit duration (5 kW x 3 h = 15 kWh).

examples.label: 10 L diesel to kg
examples.notes: A cross-dimension target answered through the fuel density.

examples.label: 1000 kWh at 0.32 EUR/kWh
examples.notes: Prices come from you, never from this tool: no tariffs are carried and no currency is converted.

examples.label: 100 m³ natural gas at 0.09 EUR/kWh
examples.notes: The heating-bill case: gas is metered in cubic metres but billed per kWh, so the calorific value sits in between.
